questions.stem: The Indian Constitution as originally adopted on 26 November 1949 had:
questions.explanation: ORIGINAL Constitution (1949) — 395 articles, 22 parts, 8 schedules. After numerous amendments + additions, current count is approximately 470+ articles (still numbered 1-395 with letter-suffixed insertions like 31A, 31B …), 25 parts (some new like IX-A Municipalities, IX-B Co-op Societies), 12 schedules. Some articles deleted (e.g., Art 31 — Right to Property, by 44th Amendment, became Art 300A). Adopted by Constituent Assembly 26 November 1949 — observed as Constitution Day. Came into force 26 January 1950 — Republic Day.

questions.stem: The 8th Schedule of the Constitution lists the:
questions.explanation: 8th Schedule — recognised Indian languages. Originally 14, now 22 — added: Sindhi (1967, 21st Amendment), Konkani+Manipuri+Nepali (1992, 71st Amendment), Bodo+Dogri+Maithili+Santhali (2003, 92nd Amendment). Demands for adding Bhojpuri, Rajasthani, Tulu, Kodava, Khasi, Garo are pending. Other key Schedules: 1 (States + UTs), 2 (emoluments), 3 (oaths), 4 (RS seat allocation), 5 (ST areas), 6 (NE tribal areas), 7 (Centre/State/Concurrent lists), 9 (laws immune to challenge — added 1st Amendment), 10 (Anti-Defection — 52nd, 1985), 11 (Panchayats — 73rd), 12 (Municipalities — 74th).

questions.stem: The 7th Schedule of the Constitution divides legislative powers into:

options.option_text: Union List, State List, Concurrent List

questions.explanation: 7th Schedule — three lists. UNION List (List I) — 100 subjects (originally 97); only Parliament can legislate (defence, foreign affairs, currency, atomic energy, posts, telecom, RBI, etc.). STATE List (List II) — 61 subjects (originally 66); only state legislature (police, public health, agriculture, local govt). CONCURRENT List (List III) — 52 subjects (originally 47); both can legislate (criminal law, marriage, succession, education — moved from State to Concurrent by 42nd Amendment). RESIDUARY POWERS rest with Centre (Art 248). Conflict in Concurrent → Union law prevails (Art 254).

questions.stem: The Constitution borrowed the FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS framework primarily from the:
questions.explanation: Sources of various features (Borrowed Constitution): (1) USA — FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS, Judicial Review, Independent Judiciary, President as head, VP, removal of judges, written Constitution. (2) UK — Parliamentary system, rule of law, single citizenship, bicameralism, cabinet responsibility, writs. (3) Ireland — DPSPs, presidential election method, RS member nomination. (4) Canada — federal structure, residuary powers with Centre. (5) Australia — concurrent list, freedom of trade. (6) Germany (Weimar) — emergency provisions. (7) South Africa — amendment procedure, RS election. (8) Japan — procedure established by law. (9) USSR — Fundamental DUTIES + planning ideal. (10) France — republic ideals.

questions.stem: The Drafting Committee of the Constitution had 7 members. The CHAIRMAN was:
questions.explanation: Drafting Committee (formed 29 August 1947) — Chairman: Dr B.R. Ambedkar. Members: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, K.M. Munshi, Saiyid Mohd Saadulla, B.L. Mitter (later N. Madhava Rau), D.P. Khaitan (later T.T. Krishnamachari). Constituent Assembly President: Rajendra Prasad. Constituent Assembly Vice-President: H.C. Mukherjee. Constitutional Adviser: B.N. Rau. Total Constituent Assembly meetings: 11 sessions, 165 days, ~3 years. Total cost ~₹6.4 crore. Original handwritten copy (in English + Hindi) by Prem Behari Narain Raizada — calligraphed; preserved in Parliament Library.

questions.stem: The Preamble to the Indian Constitution describes India as:

options.option_text: Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic (latter 2 added by 42nd Amendment, 1976)

questions.explanation: Original Preamble (1950) — 'SOVEREIGN DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC'. 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'SOCIALIST' and 'SECULAR' between Sovereign and Democratic, and 'INTEGRITY' after 'unity'. So current — 'SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC'. Other Preamble objectives: Justice — social, economic, political; Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith, worship; Equality of status and opportunity; Fraternity assuring dignity of the individual + unity and integrity of the Nation. SC in Kesavananda (1973) and Berubari (1960) cases said Preamble is part of Constitution and reflects basic structure but is not justiciable.

questions.stem: Part III of the Constitution (Articles 12-35) deals with:
questions.explanation: Part III — FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS (Art 12-35). 6 Rights now (Right to Property removed by 44th Amendment, 1978; became Art 300A — legal right): (1) Right to Equality (14-18); (2) Right to Freedom (19-22); (3) Right against Exploitation (23-24); (4) Right to Freedom of Religion (25-28); (5) Cultural & Educational Rights (29-30); (6) Right to Constitutional Remedies (32). Other key Parts: I (Union & territory, 1-4); II (Citizenship, 5-11); III (FR, 12-35); IV (DPSP, 36-51); IV-A (Fundamental Duties, 51A); V (Union government); VI (States); VIII (UTs); IX (Panchayats); IX-A (Municipalities); etc.
